findings.title: The 'Mode B — other cells' scenario enumerates three outcomes for a table that now has four, and never names the concluded-header edge
findings.recommendation: The re-entry table gained a row on the walk (no staging, active change WITHOUT explore.md → Mode B new IN the change directory) and the edge paragraph gained the concluded-header-in-change-directory case, but the scenario's THEN still reads 're-entry stated, resume in place, or refusal naming both paths'. A scenario that enumerates outcomes is a second statement of the table; either make the THEN point ('the re-entry table and its edge paragraph govern') without listing outcomes, or list all four (re-entry stated, resume in place, new in the change directory, refusal) plus the edge. Pointing is the R-crc-14 shape.

findings.title: The parity test's 'exactly one owner' rule fails the suite for any future change that legitimately MODIFIES an owned block
findings.recommendation: ownerText() requires exactly one file among the baseline and the active deltas to hold each block. After archive the baseline holds them; the moment a later change (rc13b is the obvious one — it touches the grammar) writes a MODIFIED delta carrying the fence, two files hold it and the test fails for that change's whole apply, even though a delta-plus-baseline pair is the normal mid-change state. Make the rule: if any ACTIVE delta holds the block it is the owner-to-be (require exactly one active delta), else the baseline; keep 'two active deltas' and 'no holder' as failures. The body mirror then tracks the delta during that change, which is the correct obligation.

findings.title: The conclude-verb paragraph restates the count-derived KNOWN limit that orbit-conventions owns — reintroduced by the walk's own fix
findings.recommendation: The walk replaced the record clauses with a pointer (fresh finding 5) and, in the same paragraph, the step-4 fix (fresh finding 7) added '(count-derived until the maturity-signal stage reads the header token — the last record on a concluded trail says explore or propose, and that is a named limit, not a defect)'. That is the KNOWN limit stated in orbit-conventions' concluded-outcome requirement (line 114), now stated twice across two capabilities — the shape the walk was deleting. Cut the parenthetical to a pointer: 'whose engine-computed counts and recommendation describe the concluded file (the interim limit is the concluded-outcome requirement's)'. The body may keep its reader-facing sentence.

commentary: This pass read only what the two walks wrote, because the pair had already read the rest: the mirror tags and parity test, D-bcs-12 and the two-entry exemplar, the four-fact table, the tightened status production, the GFM clause, the corollary, and every ripple. The pattern is rc02's, one level down: each walk answers a finding by adding a sentence, and the sentence is a new surface. The step-4 fix re-stated the very limit the neighbouring fix had just turned into a pointer; the fourth-fact fix widened the table but not the scenario that enumerates its outcomes; the parity instrument encodes today's state (one holder) rather than the invariant (one owner, delta preferred while a change is open), which the next change to touch the grammar would trip. None of these is a defect in the shipped behaviour and none breaks a user path — they are the same instrument-narrower-than-the-thing shape both halves of the pair named, now in the walk's additions rather than the apply's. I also corrected my own record on this pass: the fresh-walk emit claimed the boot touchpoint divergence was clear before I had read the right key; after the walk it shows one unsatisfied prediction, the architecture doc, which is the archive-tail edit. The residue sweep caught the exploration record's titles and the proposal's Impact, which no checker sees: titles and prose are not productions. What I did not do is re-execute the concluded-directory probes both independent reviewers ran; the walk changed prose around that behaviour, not the engine, and the two measurements stand.
